name: Ringo Information Kiosk (Mobile)
description: A small autonomous wheeled kiosk that roams Tier 1-2 districts offering directions, transit schedules, weather updates, and advertising — all provided free by Ringo in exchange for the facial recognition data, voice samples, and location tracking it collects from every person who interacts with it. The kiosks are friendly, helpful, and covered in cheerful Ringo branding. They are also the densest surveillance network in the lower tiers, capturing more data per day than Axiom's dedicated surveillance drones. Ringo's information kiosks know where everyone is. They just smile about it.
capacity: No passengers. Screen and speaker interface only.
range: 18 hours per charge, auto-return to charging station
autonomy: Fully autonomous, route optimization based on foot traffic density
armament: None. The data it collects is weapon enough.
common_usage: Public information service, wayfinding, advertising delivery, passive surveillance for Ringo's data brokerage.
story_hooks: A Ringo kiosk approaches a specific individual every day and displays a message that isn't in its content library — someone is using the kiosk network to communicate
A hacker cracks a kiosk's data cache and finds it has been building facial recognition profiles of every person in the district for three years
